given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans are lent on 03-02, so they fall due on 03-16, and the clock is then set to 03-17.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The test starts with a fresh database that has no reminders.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must hold each loan's memberId, loanId and dueOn, and exactly two entries.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table must hold each loan_id with sent_on 2026-03-17, and exactly two rows.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so loan1 already has a reminder recorded on the second run.
loan2 is overdue and is then returned.
loan3 is lent on 03-03, so it is due exactly on today (03-17), which tests the boundary.

then.why: Only loan1 is sent, once, across the two runs, so a send for the returned loan, the not-yet-due loan, or a repeat send would fail.

given.why: `refuseFor` makes the fake refuse loan1 with a reason.
B5 proves that a failed connection becomes a refusal, and the service test only ever sees that refusal.

then.why: The reminders table must hold only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: `toContainEqual` matches the exact level, event, loanId and error.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 is lent after loan1, which is refused, and loan2 must still be sent.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must have level info and event reminders.finished.
`objectContaining({ sent: 2 })` never checks `failed`, so a missing or wrong failed count would still pass even though one loan is refused.

given.why: A reminder with memberId, loanId and dueOn is sent through the real client.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: loan-overdue, data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The captured method, path, content-type and full body are compared with `toEqual`.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives a refusal whose reason contains "400".

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives a refusal whose reason contains "unreachable".
